visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A middle-aged man with short dark hair and glasses, wearing a black button-down shirt, speaks directly into the camera. He is positioned in a studio with a warm aesthetic, featuring bookshelves filled with books, small plants, and a partial view of a skeletal anatomical model in the background. His facial expressions are highly animated, ranging from intense focus to smiles, and he uses frequent hand gestures to punctuate his points. (2) The scene transitions to a white-screen graphic displaying a scientific research paper from the British Ecological Society. The text is dense and includes titles about wolf reintroduction in Scotland. This is followed by a map of the Scottish Highlands with various regions highlighted in purple, green, yellow, and blue, representing potential zones for ecological restoration. (3) The man returns to the frame, continuing his energetic presentation. He remains in the same medium shot, but his gestures become more expansive as he describes ecological processes. The lighting remains bright and focused on him, with a soft yellow glow from a light fixture visible on the left side of the frame. (4) A brief montage of cutaway shots appears. First, a shot of a crowd of tourists standing near a white vehicle in a natural park setting, many are holding cameras. Then, a cinematic shot of a grey wolf walking calmly through a grassy, sun-drenched forest area. These images provide visual context for the success of wildlife reintroduction in Yellowstone. (5) Back in the studio, the man continues talking. Two small image insets appear on either side of his head: one showing a group of horses grazing and the other showing several deer in a meadow. He uses his hands to point toward these images as he explains the impact of herbivores on the forest floor. (6) A digital screenshot of a news article is shown, featuring a headline about UK politicians ruling out the reintroduction of wolves and lynx. A photo of a wolf in its natural habitat is included in the article layout. (7) The video concludes with the man delivering a final question to the audience. He leans slightly forward, looking directly at the viewer with a thoughtful expression. In the final second, he points both index fingers toward the bottom of the screen to encourage user interaction or checking the comments.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Linear: Hook -> Historical Context -> Scientific Proposal -> Successful Example -> Challenges -> Local Context -> Call to Action
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to educate the audience on the concept of 'trophic cascades' by exploring the reintroduction of wolves in Scotland. It presents scientific findings suggesting that bringing wolves back could help restore forests by managing overpopulated deer and horse numbers, using the success of Yellowstone National Park as a key case study. The narrative balances these ecological benefits against the concerns of farmers and politicians, ultimately prompting viewers to consider the implications of reintroducing clouded leopards in Taiwan.
